subject: Upgrade window, modular feature staging, and pricing constraints
messages:
From: Sara Peterson <sara.peterson@luminahealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-04-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on upgrade windows and feature bundling for pilot

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The leadership team wants clarity on a couple of packaging items before we sign the pilot SOW:

1) We expect to need an upgrade mid-pilot from Compact to Core if results look good. Does Redwood support a mid-contract tier swap with proration, and how long is the earliest possible effective date?
2) We plan to turn on a small set of "enterprise" features (private routing + extended audit logs) only for a subset of 5 users initially. Can those features be added as an addon scoped to a seat pool, or do we need to upgrade the whole account?
3) Any flexibility on seat credits if we convert pilot usage to committed reserved capacity within 60 days?

We'd also like to understand what the discounting cadence looks like for mid-contract upgrades — leadership is sensitive to receiving a fair floor when switching tiers.

Attached our internal procurement checklist (small excerpt).

Sara Peterson
Head of Procurement, Lumina Health

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Peterson <sara.peterson@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-03T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on upgrade windows and feature bundling for pilot

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I added a few operational notes and a small chart attached (pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx).

Short answers:
- Mid-contract tier swap: yes. We support effective-date swaps with pro-rated billing. Earliest effective date is the start of the next billing cycle once the amendment is countersigned (typically 7–10 business days after countersignature for hosted tenants).
- Scoped feature addons: we can enable private routing + extended audit logs for a subset of seats via a seat-tagging addon. That lets you license only the 5 users initially. There are minimums for certain security features (usually 3 seats) — you're above that.
- Seat credits and reserved capacity conversion: we can apply a conversion credit for pilot consumption against the first month's reserved commitment if conversion happens within 60 days. Exact credit depends on committed term/size.

Operational notes:
- If you expect a likely upgrade window mid-pilot, we recommend establishing an "upgrade amendment" at signature to lock in agreed list prices and the conversion credit formula. That helps avoid back-and-forth later and gives your CFO predictability.
- For the seat-scoped addon we will need: a list of seat email addresses (or a seat tag) and indication whether those seats require private VPC/networking. If VPC is needed, lead time increases (~3–4 weeks).

Ben, copying you to confirm cadence on discounting and whether Sales Ops needs to run this through an exception.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Sara Peterson <sara.peterson@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on upgrade windows and feature bundling for pilot

Sara / Alex — quick from pricing ops:

- Discounting cadence: for mid-contract tier swaps we follow the calendar below:
  * If upgrade occurs within 30 days of initial signature: floor discount (pilot-to-commit) = up to 25% on list for the first 3 months, subject to term.
  * 31–60 days: up to 15% one-time credit applied to first invoice post-conversion.
  * >60 days: standard renewal discounts apply, no guaranteed conversion credit.

- The recommended approach is Alex's suggestion: include an amendment at SOW time that defines the conversion-credit formula. I'll draft a short clause we can attach to the SOW that automates the math.

- Attachments: pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx includes the scenario table (pilot consumption -> credit -> converted committed rate). Marissa, please confirm whether the seat-tagging implementation will require any additional engineering work for seat pools.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Peterson <sara.peterson@luminahealth.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on upgrade windows and feature bundling for pilot

Hey Sara — operational context from CS/Onboarding: 

- Seat-tagging + feature scoping is supported out-of-the-box for hosted customers. We'll need a kickoff call to collect the 5-seat list, confirm seat roles (admin/non-admin), and set up the feature flags. That call typically takes 45 minutes.
- If you want private routing for only those 5 seats, we treat that as an "inbound routing exception" and route through a scoped tunnel. Lead time 10 business days if no VPC required.
- If you prefer the minimal friction route, enable the seat addon for the 5 users and run the pilot on hosted with audit logs enabled. Then convert to Dedicated if you outgrow the shared pool — both paths are supported.

I'll propose times for the kickoff in a separate invite. Also attaching a redline-ready amendment (proposed_amendment_Lumina_v1.pdf) with the clause Ben mentioned. Alex / Ben please review the credit table numbers in the XLSX and confirm we can ship the redline.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
